audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-focused specifications: transaction authorization (EIP-107), state management (Cancun state.py), EVM precompiles (ALT_BN128, BLS12-381, BLAKE2F), transaction validation (EIP-2681 nonce limits, EIP-2 signature validation, EIP-7675 retroactive invariants), EL-to-CL request framework (EIP-7685), gas harmonization (EIP-8007), system opcodes (CREATE/CALL/SELFDESTRUCT), new opcodes (EIP-7880 EXTCODEADDRESS), and consensus fork management (EIP-2387 Muir Glacier).

in_scope: State Management (snapshots, accounts, storage, transient storage)
Transaction Validation (nonce limits, signature s-value, gas limits)
System Opcodes (CREATE, CREATE2, CALL variants, SELFDESTRUCT)

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions with invalid nonces, high s-values, excessive gas limits; craft precompile inputs for DoS (BLS12-381 pairing with many elements, BLAKE2F with max rounds); exploit EIP-107 popup authorization UI spoofing
Eclipse attacks, propagate blocks with incorrect difficulty calculations, send blocks violating fork activation rules

Exploit precompile input validation gaps, trigger stack depth attacks, abuse SELFDESTRUCT semantics, manipulate CREATE2 address collisions, submit crafted cryptographic inputs to BLS12/BN128 precompiles

cl_vectors.threat: Propose blocks with forged EIP-7685 requests_hash, attempt to inject invalid EL requests into CL processing
Provide incorrect data, censorship, denial of service

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions via public JSON-RPC endpoints. No authentication required. All transaction data (nonce, signature, gas limit, calldata, value) must be fully validated. This is the ultimate source of all contract calls including precompile invocations (ALT_BN128, BLS12-381, BLAKE2F), system opcode executions (CREATE/CREATE2/CALL/SELFDESTRUCT), and EIP-7685 request generation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Web DApp via Browser RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Web applications communicate with Ethereum nodes via browser-based RPC (EIP-107). DApps can submit arbitrary transaction parameters and RPC method names. The authorization popup mechanism provides user consent but the DApp itself is untrusted. Read-only RPC via iframe is filtered by a whitelist of 43 methods.

trusted_external_entities.name: End User via Authorization UI
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Human users authorize transactions via popup UI. Users may be deceived by UI spoofing attacks, phishing, or social engineering. The user's decision (approve/reject) is trusted as an intent signal but the user cannot be trusted to verify all transaction details correctly.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes propagate blocks that must be validated against consensus rules including fork activation (EIP-2387 Muir Glacier at block 9,200,000), difficulty adjustment, and all transaction validity rules. Peers are unauthenticated and can be malicious.

trusted_external_entities.name: Delegated User Account via EIP-7702
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EIP-7880 EXTCODEADDRESS opcode / EIP-7702 delegation designation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Accounts with EIP-7702 delegation designations interact with sponsorship contracts. The delegation status can change between transactions, creating race condition risks. The delegated-to address must be verified via EXTCODEADDRESS before trusting the delegation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL communicates with the EL via JWT-authenticated Engine API. While the channel is authenticated, the CL may relay data from untrusted validators. EIP-7685 requests flow from EL to CL; the CL validates and processes them. The requests_hash in block headers provides integrity but CL must independently validate request contents.

trusted_external_entities.name: EL Request Producer (Smart Contracts)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Smart contracts on the EL generate requests (via system contracts or events) that flow to the CL for processing. These requests are committed via SHA256 hash in block headers. The CL must validate all request contents independently as the generating contracts are untrusted.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: signature s-value <= secp256k1n/2 (EIP-2), nonce < 2^64-1 (EIP-2681), gas limit <= 2^63-1 (EIP-7675/EIP-4803), sender is EOA not contract (EIP-3607/EIP-7675), valid transaction encoding. All calldata bytes contribute to gas cost at 15/60 gas per zero/non-zero byte (EIP-8007/EIP-7976).

Transaction parameters (from, to, gas, gasPrice) must be validated. Method must be eth_sendTransaction (eth_sign prohibited). Read-only iframe requests filtered against 43-method whitelist. Browser same-origin policy assumed to enforce domain isolation.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EIP-107 Read-Only RPC via iframe postMessage
boundary_edges.security_assumption: RPC method must be in allowedMethods whitelist. JSON-RPC request must be parseable. Methods requiring account unlock are rejected.
User approval triggers 3-second account unlock window. Authorization popup must accurately display transaction details. UI spoofing must be prevented by the browser environment.

Blocks must be validated against fork-specific consensus rules. For Muir Glacier (EIP-2387): verify block number >= 9,200,000 triggers EIP-2384 difficulty bomb delay. Difficulty calculation must use correct fake block number offset. All transactions in block must pass all validation rules.

All precompile inputs arrive via transactions from untrusted users. ALT_BN128: validate input length (64/128/192*n bytes), field element < modulus, point on curve, subgroup membership. BLS12-381: validate input length per operation type, field elements < BLS12 modulus, point on curve, subgroup check (point * curve_order == infinity). BLAKE2F: validate input exactly 213 bytes, final flag in {0,1}. Gas must be correctly charged before execution.

All system opcode invocations originate from user transactions. Must validate: init code size <= MAX_INIT_CODE_SIZE, address collision checks (EIP-7610 storage collision), call depth <= 1024, sender nonce < 2^64-1, sender balance >= endowment/value, static context restrictions for value transfer and SELFDESTRUCT. EIP-6780: SELFDESTRUCT only deletes contracts created in same transaction.

EXTCODEADDRESS resolves only one level of delegation. Delegation target is NOT warmed (subsequent cold access costs apply). Sponsorship contracts must verify delegation target against whitelist. Delegation can change between transactions (TOCTOU risk).
JWT authentication validates channel but payload content must be validated. Block payloads must pass all EL validation rules. The CL is trusted for fork choice but not for payload correctness.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EIP-7685 Request Processing via Engine API
boundary_edges.security_assumption: CL must independently validate all request contents. requests_hash (SHA256) in block header provides integrity commitment. Requests sorted by type ascending; empty requests excluded from hash. CL rejection does not affect EL block validity. Each request type has its own validation rules defined by subsequent EIPs.
